content:
We need to propose a 3-step retrosynthesis for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: steps are (forward) 1) amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine (coupling). 2) Doebner modification to form α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid. 3) sulfonamide formation from amine + sulfonyl chloride.

Thus retrosynthetic direction: target -> break amide to give acid and aniline (aniline attached to phenyl). The amide is C(=O)N attached to aniline (c3ccccc3N). So disconnection: target amide carbonyl from carboxylic acid precursor (α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (aniline). So step 1 retrosynthesis: target -> precursor acid (with α,β-unsaturated acid) + aniline (c3ccccc3N). The acid is the α,β-unsaturated acid attached to phenyl sulfonyl aryl group? Actually the amide is attached to the unsaturated chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-aryl. The acid precursor would be /C=C/C(=O)OH (cinnamic acid derivative) attached to phenyl sulfonyl aryl? Wait the sulfonamide is attached to the first phenyl ring (para-methyl phenyl) with NS(=O)(=O) attached to second phenyl ring which bears the unsaturated chain. So the amide is on the unsaturated chain attached to second phenyl ring. So disconnection: break amide to give cinnamic acid (with phenyl sulfonyl attached) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So step 1: amide formation.

Step 2: The cinnamic acid precursor can be formed via Doebner modification from aromatic aldehyde (p-methyl phenyl sulfonyl phenyl aldehyde?) Actually the aromatic aldehyde is the phenyl ring bearing sulfonyl group and aldehyde at para position relative? The target has c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)...)cc2 attached to sulfonyl group. So the aldehyde precursor would be the same aromatic ring with aldehyde instead of the unsaturated chain: c2ccc(CHO)cc2 attached to sulfonyl group. So step 2: Doebner modification of that aldehyde with malonic acid to give the α,β-unsaturated acid.

Step 3: Sulfonamide formation: the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be the sulfonyl chloride attached to the first phenyl ring (p-methyl phenyl) and the second phenyl ring (the one that later gets aldehyde). Actually sulfonamide formation is between an amine (the first phenyl ring's amine) and sulfonyl chloride (attached to second phenyl). In target, the sulfonamide is NS(=O)(=O) linking the two phenyl rings. So retrosynthesis: break sulfonamide to give aniline (first phenyl) and sulfonyl chloride attached to second phenyl (aryl sulfonyl chloride). So step 3: sulfonamide formation.

Thus overall three steps.

Now we need to produce JSON route with three reaction nodes.

We need template IDs for each transformation. We have some templates from earlier search: template 733 is sulfonamide formation (Cl-SO2-aryl + aniline -> sulfonamide). That matches our sulfonamide step. So we can use template_id 733.

For amide formation, need a template that couples carboxylic acid to amine. Search for amide formation template. Let's search for functional_groups_formed "amide".
